llm.rationale: The pattern suggests prioritizing tests to provide earlier failure feedback. In this workflow, there are many independent 'Test Suite' jobs. While the pattern is typically applied to individual test cases within a single job, in a GitHub Actions context with many parallel jobs, we can simulate prioritization by reordering the jobs in the YAML. I will move the 'Test Suite [all features]' job (which is likely the most comprehensive and thus most likely to catch regressions) to the top of the list of test jobs to ensure it is queued/started as early as possible, although GitHub's scheduler may still parallelize them. This adheres to the requirement of implementing the mechanism even if the benefit is uncertain.
